title: Totally True History (Mostly)
blurb: Kings, presidents, inventors and candy bars. Three facts per card, and one is cap.

cards.say: [The first basketball game was played with a soccer ball], [Benjamin Franklin asked Congress to make the turkey the national bird], [Abraham Lincoln is honored in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame], and [a sheep, a duck and a rooster were the first passengers in a hot air balloon].
cards.real: Franklin praised the turkey in a letter to his daughter, but he never asked for it to become a national symbol.

cards.say: [The first Ferris wheel, built in 1893, was America's answer to the Eiffel Tower], [Toblerone's name mixes its maker's family name with an Italian word for nougat], [the first Olympic champion on record, about 2,800 years ago, was a cook], and [Viking warriors wore metal helmets with big horns sticking out].
cards.real: There's no evidence Vikings wore horned helmets. That look comes from opera costumes made in the 1870s.

cards.say: [Knights in heavy armor had to be lifted onto their horses with cranes], [Benjamin Harrison and his wife were too scared to touch the White House light switches], [King Henry VIII's palace had one giant toilet room that could seat 28 people], and [Pluto was named by an 11-year-old girl from England].
cards.real: Knights could climb onto their horses by themselves. A full suit of plate armor usually weighed about 45 to 55 pounds.

cards.say: [A flock of sheep once trimmed the White House lawn], [William Taft became the first president to throw out a baseball first pitch, in 1910], [George Washington's false teeth were carved out of wood], and [the Palace of Versailles started out as a hunting lodge].
cards.real: Washington never had wooden teeth. His false teeth were made from things like hippo ivory, metal and real teeth.

cards.say: [Napoleon was much shorter than most men of his time], [Ken and Barbie were named after their inventor's real children], [President Calvin Coolidge kept a raccoon named Rebecca as a pet], and [merchants were writing the @ sign almost 500 years ago].
cards.real: Napoleon was about 5 feet 6 inches, above average for his time. Old French inches were longer, which confused people.

cards.say: [Mount Rushmore was meant to show the presidents down to their waists], [Hershey's chocolate bars sold for five cents each until the year 1999], [Louis Braille was 15 when he came up with his reading system for blind people], and [Theodore Roosevelt's kids kept a badger and a one-legged rooster at the White House].
cards.real: The five-cent Hershey's bar ended in 1969. After that, a bigger bar that cost ten cents became the standard.

cards.say: [Caroline Herschel, an astronomer in the 1700s, discovered eight comets], [Alan Turing wrote a chess program in 1948 that no computer back then could run], [Lincoln Logs were invented by the son of the architect Frank Lloyd Wright], and [the teddy bear, first made in 1902, was named after Franklin Roosevelt].
cards.real: The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt, whose nickname was Teddy.

cards.say: [The Liberty Bell cracked the first time it was rung in Philadelphia], [the Eiffel Tower was only supposed to stand for 20 years], [you can see the Great Wall of China from the Moon with your own eyes], and [Herbert Hoover, in 1929, was the first president with a phone on his desk].
cards.real: The Great Wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon. Even from low orbit, astronauts can barely spot it, if at all.

cards.say: [People in ancient Pompeii bought hot food at street counters, like fast food], [Cadbury Dairy Milk chocolate was almost named Dairy Maid], [Sacagawea carried her baby son along on the Lewis and Clark expedition], and [ancient Romans built special rooms for throwing up at big feasts].
cards.real: A vomitorium was really a passageway that let crowds pour in and out of a Roman amphitheater.

cards.say: [The scientist Albert Einstein failed math when he was a boy in school], [Leonardo da Vinci designed a robot knight more than 500 years ago], [the Game Boy's designer started out fixing machines in Nintendo's card factory], and [James Garfield gave part of a campaign speech in German before he became president].
cards.real: Einstein was great at math. He taught himself algebra and geometry at about 12 and said he had mastered calculus before he was 15.

cards.say: [The Mona Lisa was stolen in 1911 and stayed missing for over two years], [William Herschel, who discovered Uranus, was a musician before he was an astronomer], [the very first solid chocolate bar was made at a factory in America], and [Benjamin Franklin invented swim fins when he was just 11 years old].
cards.real: The first solid chocolate bar was made in England in 1847 by Joseph Fry of the J.S. Fry & Sons chocolate company.

cards.say: [The man who created Pokémon was nicknamed Dr. Bug as a kid], [a recording of Abraham Lincoln's voice still exists today], [the inventor of basketball had a losing record as a college coach], and [President William Taft kept a cow named Pauline at the White House].
cards.real: No recording of Lincoln's voice exists. He died in 1865, twelve years before Thomas Edison invented the phonograph in 1877.
